biography.plain_text: August Anheuser Busch Jr., known as Gussie, was an American brewing executive who expanded his family’s Anheuser-Busch business into a national industry leader. Succeeding his older brother as president, he developed a network of regional breweries and promoted Budweiser through mass advertising. Executive leadership later passed to his son, August Busch III.

long_biography.plain_text:
When Anheuser-Busch bought the St. Louis Cardinals in 1953, August Busch Jr. became the baseball club’s president. The purchase kept the team in St. Louis when relocation was a possibility. He later helped bring a new downtown stadium into being, giving the brewery-owned club a more modern home and maintaining his family’s visible association with the city.

Busch remained involved in baseball after stepping away from the brewery’s daily management. During his long presidency, the Cardinals won three World Series championships. His appearances at games became part of the spectacle: he rode into the stadium on a wagon pulled by the Budweiser Clydesdales, waving a red cowboy hat to the crowd.
